<reason>CON won by making the motion fail its own test: aquifer and tap outcomes are about litres, and a ban on corporate bottling identity leaves larger, substitutable withdrawals untouched. PRO’s civic-merchandise frame stayed vivid and locally pointed, but it never resolved the hole-versus-total-ban tension, the label/substitution problem, or why caps would bind farms and fabs yet fail only against bottlers. Virtual-water export then collapsed the input-versus-cargo distinction.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s capture-and-label sequence: a state too weak to meter a watched wellhead cannot magically enforce a bottling ban, and if caps restrain almonds and fabs, distrusting them only against the smallest user is villainy, not hydrology.</best_rebuttal>
